title: Review the use of Google Analytics
body:
# What data do we want?

Most data related with our audience/page view. For example,

- When do your users visit?
- Where are your users?
- What pages do your users visit?
- How are your active users trending over time?
- What are your top devices?

# Why do we need that data?

1. To provide numbers for funders
2. To assist when making decisions

# Why do we need to review it uses?

Although we collect the data, isn't clear who is the gate keeper for it. Most of the data that we collect with Google Analytics could make public and avoid maintainers and other volunteers to ask around how to access that data.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Note: I am not a lawyer, but this is my understanding of how this works.

## Possible violation of GDPR, without cookie banners

I see that this issue was created around the time GDPR was implemented in the EU and has not been discussed ever since. A caveat of using Google Analytics is that without _explicit user consent being requested via annoying cookie banners_ at every lesson, the Carpentries would be in _violation of GDPR._

## Alternatives exist

Open source solutions (such as Matomo and Plausible) which do not track personally identifiable information would 

1. be better suited for an organization of such standing
2. respect the user's privacy
3. have possiblity to self-host
4. not need cookie banners

## References

- https://matomo.org/cookie-consent-banners/
- https://matomo.org/blog/2018/04/how-to-not-process-any-personal-data-with-matomo-and-what-it-means-for-you/
- https://plausible.io/vs-matomo

comments.body:
Thanks for bringing this up @ashwinvis. We are in the process of overhauling our privacy policy and cookies policy and we'll soon have further details available about this.

We are in the process of converting all our analytics to using the cookie-less version of Matomo, and I did so in 25a5b9f for the lesson template.
